newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga meets board over Santa Fe, no comment on deal.
newsitem.headline: Saga meets board over Santa Fe, no comment on deal.

text.p: The management of Norway's Saga Petroleum ASA met with its supervisory board on Monday about the purchase of Santa Fe Exploration Ltd, but declined to say if the final go-ahead for the deal had been given.
But Saga spokesman Andreas Qvale told Reuters the meeting, which ended around 2030 GMT, was one of the last formalities and the company hoped to have a news conference first thing on Tuesday.
"Most of it is settled. If there are no other problems to solve we aim to have a press conference tomorrow," Qvale said.
Market sources in London said Saga was expected to clinch British-based Santa Fe from state-owned Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) for $1.2 billion (7.72 billion crowns).

Saga declined to provide a figure, but if confirmed, the deal will be the second largest acquisition by a Norwegian company following Kvaerner's takeover of British conglomerate Trafalgar House Plc in April for 8.9 billion crowns.
Share trading in Norway's largest independent oil company was suspended from the Oslo bourse on Monday pending an announcement of the takeover.
Santa Fe has interests in over 40 UK offshore blocks and 25 blocks off Ireland. Its production levels reached a high of over 60,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day in 1995.
KPC announced in June it would sell the North Sea exploration group. ($1=6.43 crowns)
